name: Complete atrioventricular septal defect without ventricular hypoplasia
aliases: Complete AV septal defect without ventricular hypoplasia
Complete atrioventricular canal defect without ventricular hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic diagnostic criteria for complete AV septal defect

criteria.description: Presence of a common atrioventricular valve with a large atrial and ventricular septal defect
Normal size and morphology of both ventricles without hypoplasia
Confirmation of defect anatomy by transthoracic or transesophageal echocardiography
Presence of signs of congestive heart failure in infancy such as tachypnea and failure to thrive

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a common atrioventricular valve with combined atrial and ventricular septal defects on echocardiography without evidence of ventricular hypoplasia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging; genetic testing may support but is not diagnostic.

pathognomonic.notes: Leads to volume overload and heart failure

pathognomonic.symptomName: Large atrial and ventricular septal defects
searchTerms: big atrial and ventricular septal defects

pathognomonic.notes: Due to left-to-right shunting and valve insufficiency

common.notes: Rapid breathing secondary to pulmonary overcirculation
Heard on auscultation due to valve abnormalities

occasional.notes: Limited physical activity in older children
Secondary to increased pulmonary blood flow

rare.notes: Rare complication due to paradoxical embolism

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing common AV valve and combined atrial and ventricular septal defects
Chest X-ray with cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomy if needed
other: Electrocardiogram showing left axis deviation and atrioventricular conduction abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of separate mitral and tricuspid valves
Smaller or absent ventricular septal defect
Isolated ventricular septal defect without atrial septal involvement

redFlags: Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Severe valve regurgitation causing hemodynamic instability
Development of pulmonary hypertension early in life
references: Anderson RH, et al. Paediatric Cardiology. 4th ed. Churchill Livingstone; 2010.
Moller JH, et al. Congenital Heart Disease: A Practical Guide. Wiley-Blackwell; 2012.
